body.x: Warp Solution Inc. (CEO Kyunghak Lee) showcased its next-generation charging infrastructure technology at CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

Warp Solution is a Korean company that has developed RF (radio frequency)-based long-range wireless power transfer (WTP) technology. Since its establishment in 2016, the company has continued to advance RF application technologies that enable multiple devices to operate without physical contact or precise alignment, with the goal of realizing next-generation power infrastructure that supplies electricity across entire spaces, the company said.

To this end, Warp Solution has independently designed and developed key semiconductor products, ranging from RF power amplification devices to high-efficiency RF-DC rectifier chips. The company explained that these technologies represent a rare case in Korea of advancing core long-range wireless charging technologies to the commercialization stage.

Warp Solution’s technology has drawn strong expectations for use in systems and infrastructure where wired power supply or frequent battery replacement poses challenges, including industrial IoT sensors, smart logistics, building automation, and healthcare equipment. Based on this technological foundation, Warp Solution introduced its next-generation WTP platform, ‘WARPS (Wireless Autonomous RF Power System),’ highlighting its technological competitiveness.

WARPS consists of an RF transmission unit that outputs power, a dedicated receiver that captures and rectifies the energy, and software algorithms that control power flow. Unlike conventional wireless chargers that require physical contact or precise alignment between the charger and device, WARPS is designed to simultaneously charge multiple devices located within a defined space without physical contact or alignment.

body.cap: Semiconductor components applied to WARPS. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: More specifically, RF energy transmitted from the RF module is converted into electrical power by the receiver, which then charges batteries or directly powers devices. At the same time, the system integrates AI-based tracking and beamforming control technologies through software, enabling real-time recognition of device locations and movement paths and dynamically adjusting the directionality and output of RF energy.

As a result, WARPS can provide stable power even to devices that move frequently or lack fixed installation points, while enabling simultaneous charging of multiple devices through efficient power distribution. Warp Solution emphasized that the use of its in-house semiconductor lineup further enhances both power delivery stability and conversion efficiency.

Warp Solution has secured broad applicability by positioning WARPS as a continuous power supply for smart logistics facilities, factory automation equipment, and healthcare devices that require frequent battery replacement or struggle to deploy wired power infrastructure. The company introduced WARPS as a next-generation power infrastructure that supplies energy on a space-by-space basis, drawing significant attention from on-site visitors.

A Warp Solution representative said, “Long-range wireless power transfer technology has now moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage and reached a level suitable for real industrial applications,” adding, “At CES, we emphasized that our technology meets the stability and continuity requirements of industrial environments and presented a new paradigm for wireless charging technology.”

The representative continued, “By demonstrating that WARPS can serve as a practical alternative for wireless, battery-free power environments across various industries, we received meaningful interest and inquiries from industry stakeholders,” adding, “We will do our utmost to turn the networks gained here into tangible results.”
